content.comment_body: Hello, we have some discontinued [company_name] [product_name] at our workplace. One of them stopped functioning properly, so we're looking to replace it with a new unit. My question is, assuming I have the correct programming cable, can I use a newer version of the software to transfer the programming from this unit to a newer one? The manual mentioned [product_name] [version_no], which appears to be for older Windows systems such as XP. I'm new to working with [company_name] devices, so the hardware numbers don't mean much to me except that this is a [company_name] product. After searching with the part number, I saw it's discontinued. Thank you in advance for any help.

Hello, I'm not certain, but it's likely that upgrading directly from an older software version to the latest may not work smoothly. I would suggest recreating the program from scratch in the newest software version. Best regards.

The latest software version will work with all generations of [product_name] devices. The main challenge is ensuring the programming cable operates on Windows 10. If you have a USB-type programming cable for the older [product_name], you should be fine. Make sure to select your hardware version in the [product_name] software before starting the upload or download process.

You can download the free upgrade to the latest [product_name] software from [url]. Note, the download is subject to export restrictions, which means you'll need to register before accessing it. Installation requires an existing full software version on your hard drive or installation media. If you have or purchase a new [product_name] unit, you'll need the latest version of the software.
